title: Tanakh
hookLine: Torah, Prophets and Writings, twenty-four books in the Jewish count

lines: A TABLE OF CONTENTS IN A WORD.
cards: One word on the spine of a Jewish Bible: Tanakh. It isn't the name of a person or a place. It's a table of contents squeezed into one word.

All along this path we've walked through it: creation and the patriarchs, Moses and the wilderness, judges and kings, prophets, poems, Job's arguments, Esther's banquet, Daniel in Babylon, Ezra and Nehemiah rebuilding.
Yesterday we turned the last page. So today, what the whole thing is called, and how it's put together.

teach.b: Tanakh is built from the first letters of its three parts: T, N, K.
T is for Torah, teaching: the books of Moses, Genesis to Deuteronomy, the scroll that sits in the ark in a synagogue and is read aloud, portion by portion.

N is for Nevi'im, Prophets: the stories of Joshua, Judges, Samuel and Kings, then the books of the prophets themselves, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, and the shorter prophets, which tradition counts together as one book called the Twelve.
K is for Ketuvim, Writings: Psalms, Proverbs and Job, the scrolls like Ruth, Esther and Ecclesiastes, then Daniel, Ezra and Nehemiah, and Chronicles at the close.

Count Samuel, Kings, the Twelve, Ezra and Nehemiah, and Chronicles each as one, and you reach the number Jewish tradition gives: twenty-four books. The Talmud also records an order for the Prophets and the Writings.
So hear Tanakh as a library with three rooms. The first is the teaching itself. The second is what happened when a people tried to live it, and the prophets who called them back.
The third is everything else a people needs: songs, wisdom, love poetry, grief, history, and hard questions.
And the rooms are used differently. The Torah is read from the scroll in order, week by week. Passages from the Prophets are read alongside it.
Some of the Writings come out on particular days, like Esther on Purim.

how: In synagogue the Torah is read from a handwritten scroll, portion by portion, in order, a passage from the Prophets called the haftarah is read with it, and some of the Writings, such as Esther on Purim, are read on particular days.

o: the Torah scroll kept in the synagogue's ark
the Hebrew Bible, named for its three parts
the Talmud, the rabbis' discussions of the law

games.q: the three letters of Tanakh — tap the pairs.
p: the shorter prophets, as one book

s: Tanakh is the name of a place
it's built from the initials of its three parts: Torah, Nevi'im, Ketuvim.
Jewish tradition counts the Tanakh as twenty-four books
Samuel, Kings, the Twelve, Ezra-Nehemiah and Chronicles each count as one.
Psalms and Job are in the Prophets
they're in the Ketuvim, the Writings.

games.q: you open a volume that holds Ruth, Esther and Ecclesiastes. which part of the Tanakh is it from?
games.why: Ruth, Esther and Ecclesiastes belong to the Ketuvim, the Writings, the third room of the library.

practice: Breathe in slowly, and on each out-breath say one name silently: Torah, teaching; Nevi'im, Prophets; Ketuvim, Writings. Go around again, and let one story you remember from this path come to mind with each room.
If you pray, give thanks in words from your tradition for something you learned from them.

wordCard.voice: Tanakh. The Hebrew Bible's own name, built from its three parts: Torah, Nevi'im and Ketuvim, teaching, Prophets and Writings. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: from the initials of Torah, Nevi'im and Ketuvim.
